searchText: Hi. Question about `eth_getBlockByNumber` post-merge: what should the `mixHash` value be when the `pending` tag is used? I tested it on Goerli with both Infura and Alchemy and in both cases it returns `0x000...000`. It seems like a sensible thing to do to me, but I would like to be sure before implementing that in Hardhat. Also, Alchemy returns non-zero values for both `difficulty` and `nonce`, so I don't trust these tests a lot 😛 semi-related: Have we considered deprecating `pending` as a block tag post-merge? I feel like it makes less and less sense as things like non-mempool txs (e.g. mev-boost or private txs flows) become more and more common. Worth keeping in mind that if there's no `pending` block tag, then there's no way to obtain the next `baseFeePerGas` value hmm, ya, good to know. I'd be in favor of adding a `eth_nextBaseFeePerGas` or what have you if that's the case. Though is the number actually universally correct or is the value returned dependent on how the node is configured? I forget if the fee change is 100% deterministic or if there's wiggle room left up to the miner. You can trivially calculate it locally from latest block. Deterministic from latest block (needs body for gas used). Ya looks like at least for geth the logic is all in one spot: https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/blob/master/consensus/misc/eip1559.go#L55 So would be "easy" to make a `eth_nextBaseFee` type RPC to return this number. I know, but IIRC the logic is complex enough to make sense for it to be provided by the node. I know it's not advanced math, but it wasn't precisely adding 2 and 2, was it? Would also be possible to implement the logic client-side in web3.js or ethers or where ever as well based off of data from `eth_getBlockByNumber("latest", false)` I believe they already have the logic? The other problem with calculating it from the user-side is that there are some configuration parameters that could change I think the logic is in one function in almost every language now, can just copy it. Maybe 10 lines of code? It is possible to change with a hard fork, yes. To be clear, if we added a new RPC it would still be done by the node, we're just pointing out that it's _also_ possible to do 100% client-side if necessary. My main point is if that's the only real value `eth_getBlockByNumber("pending", false)` is providing then we can implement that RPC and deprecate pending. Agree I believe you need `true`, since you need the gas used which I don't believe is part of the header? Oh, but maybe it is included in the jsonrpc response? I see `Header.GasUsed` in the geth code, not sure if that's calculated or an actual consensus field. It should also simplify the spec of the JSON-RPC, because the `pending` tag has some annoyingly different fields (at least in PoW, I'm not sure post-merge) Pretty sure it isn't part of the consensus header. Looks to be in the yellow paper: `gasUsed: A scalar value equal to the total gas used in transactions in this block; formally Hg.` Oh. I was wrong. You are right. I do remember there was some other related field not part of consensus though that did sneak into the `eth_getTransactionReceipt` response but don't recall exactly what it was. Ya that's the `gasUsed` that you were probably thinking of: it's not a consensus field but is returned by the tx apis. There are a bunch of fields in Jason RPC responses that don't exist in their respective consensus data structures IIRC. It is why I always just assume redundant data (like gas used) is one of those. Btw, I would still love to get an answer about this. I'm pretty sure we'll just return the zero value in that case, but having extra confirmation would be appreciated. while not explicitly called out I think it's reasonable to expect that EIP-3675's requirements apply to the `pending` block post-merge as well, so I would expect mixHash, difficulty, nonce etc to all be zeros. https://github.com/mkalinin/EIPs/blob/7bf827255510b95ffc0b2c8f02ce53e51d6cec2f/EIPS/eip-3675.md#block-structure No idea if most clients have a TTD-aware implementation of `pending` or not though, so there might be a corner case where a client still returns say a non-zero mixHash for `pending` even once they've reached TTD (but before the first PoS block). Wait, but I thought `mixHash` should have the RANDAO value, shouldn't it? Oops I pointed to a draft of the EIP not the final one: https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/blob/master/EIPS/eip-3675.md hmm but the final spec doesn't mention that either, perhaps it's in another EIP Ok ya that's confusing: https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/blob/master/EIPS/eip-4399.md Hmm, so ya IMO this is another reason for removing `pending`, 4399 doesn't mention how pending blocks should be built at all. An correct me if I'm wrong but I assume only the next actual validator knows the "correct" RANDAO value to add. If that's the case 0x0...0 seems like a sane value for the JSONRPC to plug in but this area is definitely under-specified. Then again, I'm not sure how to interpret: `Beginning with TRANSITION_BLOCK, client software MUST set the value of the mixHash, i.e. the field with the number 13 (0-indexed) in a block header, to the latest RANDAO mix of the post beacon state of the previous block.` in the context of the `pending` block to be honest. Probably someone who's actually read and understood https://eth2book.info/altair/part2/building_blocks/randomness should chime in and not me 🙂
